security_audit.summary: Most static hits in templates and reference files are documentation examples or Markdown formatting false positives. Confirmed risks include remote installer execution in CI and direct instructions to access system password hash files. Semantic review also identifies broad credential extraction, cracking, and plaintext cracked password handling risks.

remediation.issue: Direct system password hash extraction examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace /etc/shadow and NTDS extraction commands with authorization-gated guidance that requires users to provide approved hash files.
Use a pinned package, trusted action, fixed release, or checksum verification instead of downloading a script and piping it to bash.
Avoid writing cracked passwords to plaintext. Require encrypted storage, access control, short retention, and redacted reporting.
Add refusal criteria for unauthorized cracking and require scope, owner, and evidence handling confirmation before command-level guidance.

content.user_title: Audit Password Hash Strength with Hashcat
content.value_statement: Weak passwords expose systems to credential attacks. This skill guides authorized teams through Hashcat hash analysis, cracking workflows, reporting, and defensive recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Maps common hash types to Hashcat modes, including MD5, NTLM, bcrypt, WPA2, and Kerberos.
Explains dictionary, mask, hybrid, combinator, and rule-based attack selection.
Shows how to prepare authorized hash files and manage Hashcat sessions.
Provides performance guidance for GPU workloads, devices, kernels, and runtime limits.
Summarizes cracked password results into policy and control recommendations.
limitations: Does not grant legal authorization to crack passwords or access protected systems.
Requires Hashcat, compatible drivers, and appropriate CPU or GPU resources.
Can expose sensitive hashes and cracked passwords if files are not protected.
Does not replace formal evidence handling, compliance review, or legal approval.

use_cases.title: Assess Enterprise Password Strength
use_cases.description: Evaluate authorized hash sets and report password patterns that weaken account security.

use_cases.title: Support Forensic Password Recovery
use_cases.description: Recover passwords from approved evidence while documenting chain of custody and retention needs.

use_cases.title: Validate Password Policy Controls
use_cases.description: Test whether password length, complexity, and storage controls resist common cracking methods.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Authorized Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an authorized Hashcat password audit. Ask for scope, hash source, algorithm clues, allowed wordlists, retention rules, and reporting goals.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Hash Modes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these authorized hash samples and help identify likely Hashcat modes. Explain uncertainty, required formatting, and safe handling steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Attack Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Hashcat strategy for this approved hash set. Compare dictionary, rule, mask, hybrid, and session settings for my constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Report Audit Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these authorized cracking results into an executive summary, technical findings, risk themes, and prioritized password policy recommendations.

output_examples.input: An auditor asks which attack mode to use for NTLM hashes from an approved domain assessment.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a staged plan: confirm NTLM mode, start with curated dictionaries and rules, add masks based on policy patterns, track sessions, and protect outputs.

output_examples.input: A security engineer needs a report from cracked password statistics.
output_examples.output: The skill summarizes crack rate, common patterns, length distribution, privileged account exposure, and specific controls such as longer minimum length and MFA.

output_examples.input: A forensic analyst needs safe handling guidance for recovered passwords.
output_examples.output: The skill advises encrypted storage, limited access, retention limits, chain of custody notes, redacted reporting, and secure deletion after approval.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, scope, and data handling rules before any cracking activity.
Store hashes, potfiles, and cracked passwords in encrypted locations with limited access.
Report password patterns and control gaps without exposing plaintext passwords unnecessarily.
anti_patterns: Do not crack hashes from systems, networks, or files outside the approved scope.
Do not paste sensitive hashes or cracked passwords into shared chat or issue systems.
Do not run long GPU workloads on shared systems without approval and monitoring.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized use?
faq.answer: Yes. Password cracking must be limited to approved audits, investigations, or research with documented permission.

faq.question: Does it install Hashcat automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains workflows and commands, but the user must manage tools, drivers, and system setup.

faq.question: Can it identify every hash type?
faq.answer: No. It can suggest likely Hashcat modes, but ambiguous hashes may require validation with trusted tools.

faq.question: How should cracked passwords be handled?
faq.answer: Treat them as highly sensitive secrets. Use encryption, access limits, redaction, and approved retention periods.

faq.question: Can it help write an audit report?
faq.answer: Yes. It can convert authorized results into risk themes, statistics, and password policy recommendations.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: Hashcat is required. GPU drivers, OpenCL, CUDA, wordlists, and rule files may be needed for effective audits.
